chunks: Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib narrated to me, saying:

I sat in wait for Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) on the roadside. When he passed by me, I complained to him of my need, and I swore to him that I did not have a single dirham or anything above it, nor any lunch nor dinner.

He said: He (عليه السلام) said, "You are swearing by Allah falsely, while you have buried two hundred dinars. What I say is not to withhold the gift from you. O servant, give him what you have." So his servant gave me one hundred dinars. Then he turned to me and said, "You will be deprived of them at the time when you are most in need of them," meaning the dinars that I had buried.

And he (عليه السلام) spoke the truth, and it happened just as he said. I had buried two hundred dinars and said, "It will be support and refuge for us." Then I was struck by intense necessity for something to spend, and the doors of livelihood were closed to me. So I dug for it, only to find that a son of mine had come to know its location, taken it, and fled, and I could not recover anything of it.

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ الرِّزْقِ: the means and openings of livelihood
key_terms.الْحَاجَةَ: need or hardship that prompted the complaint
key_terms.تُحْرَمُهَا: you will be deprived of it
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: gold coin; a unit of wealth

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the truthfulness and divine knowledge of Imam Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter with Imam Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام), in which he reveals hidden knowledge about a man's buried wealth and still grants him financial assistance. It also recounts the fulfillment of the Imam's warning that the man would be deprived of that buried money at the time of greatest need, highlighting both the Imam's truthfulness and the moral gravity of false oaths.

en.hubeali: Is’haq said, ‘Ismail Bin Muhammad Bin Ali Bin Ismail Bin Ali Bin Abdullah Bin Abbas Bin Abdul Muttalib narrated to me saying,

‘I saw (awaiting) for Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> (11<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>) upon the back of the road. So when he<sup>asws</sup> passed by me, I complained to him<sup>asws</sup> of the need and I swore on oath to him<sup>asws</sup> that there wasn’t a (single) Dirham with me and what was above it, nor any lunch nor a dinner’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘You swore on oath with Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a lie, and you have buried two hundred Dinars, and this word of mine<sup>asws</sup> isn’t to repel you from the granting. O boy! Give him what is with you!’ So his<sup>asws</sup> servant gave me two hundred Dinars’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> turned towards me, and he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘You will be deprived of it when you are as needy to it as can happen to be, meaning the Dinars which you have buried’.

And he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> spoke the truth, and it happenned just as he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said. I had buried two hundred Dinars and I said, ‘It will happen to be a backing and a cave for us’. Then I was desperate with an intense necessity to something (I needed) to spend, and the doors of the sustenance were closed upon me. So I went to exhume it, and it was so that a son of mine had recognised its place, so he had taken it and fled, and I was not able upon anything from it’.
en.sarwar: 14. Ishaq has said that narrated to him ’Isma‘il ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Ali ibn ‘Abdallah ibn ‘Abbass ibn ‘Abd al-Muttalib who has said the following.

“Once I sat on the side of the road waiting for abu Muhammad (a.s.) to pass by so that I can present before him my complain against a need. When he was passing by I presented my complain before him and swore that I did not have even a Dirham, nothing for lunch or dinner.”

The narrator has said that the Imam (a.s.) said, “You falsely swore by Allah. You have buried two hundred Dinars. These my words are not to deny you any grants. Young man, give him whatever is with you. His servant, give me one hundred Dinars. He then turned to me and said, “You will be deprived of it in your worst days.” He meant those Dinars that I had buried for a difficult day.

What he said was true. I had buried two hundred Dinars thinking that they would only be used in a very difficult day. When I faced such a difficult day and all the ways to find a living was closed I went to take out the two hundred Dinars but soon I found that there was not even a single Dinar. In fact, my son had learned about where the Dinars were buried and he had taken them and had ran away. I could not benefit from any of those Dinars.”
